title: healthz starved for minutes under heavy code-source ingest
wanted_capability: The liveness surface (/healthz) should answer within its probe timeout regardless of ingest load. During a large code-source batch (one generation of 4.6k files / 1.5GB among a multi-project sweep), /healthz stopped answering within 5s for over two minutes, so the orchestrator killed a healthy daemon mid-activation and tore a multi-store update (the 2026-08-13 boot-refusal outage). The plane-isolation model (design/daemon-runtime/concurrency-model.md) intends the HTTP plane to stay responsive while ingest runs; either a blocking section in the ingest/activation path is riding the serving runtime, or /healthz shares a resource (lock, runtime, IO pool) with ingest that it should not. Wanted: identify the starvation mechanism (tokio blocking, held lock, fs contention on the PVC) and isolate the health endpoint so it answers from cheap process-local state; secondarily consider a load-shedding readiness signal distinct from liveness so heavy ingest degrades to not-ready instead of dead.
missing_primitive: ingest-independent liveness answer (health from process-local state, no shared locks/runtime with ingest)
fallback_used: Raised cage probe tolerance (liveness 15s timeout, 15 failures at 20s period, bbox-cage 6694a11) so a busy daemon is not killed; treats the symptom, not the starvation.
evidence: crates/bbox-indexing/src/code_source_locality_manifest.rs (write-ordering doc born from the torn update)
notes: Sequence from the incident: 04:37Z collector uploads a multi-project code-source batch; 04:39Z liveness probes time out repeatedly; orchestrator kills the daemon mid-activation; boot then refuses on the torn journal/manifest pair (fixed by the reconciliation sweep). The probe tolerance change makes recurrence unlikely to kill, but the underlying starvation still degrades every MCP caller during ingest windows.
